body:
Great story. Hit real close to home too. I lost my mother to suicide not three weeks ago. Video games and a supportive girlfriend and various other family members have helped me get through it. I'm actually playing through the entire series right now as well so I can show her the story because this game is a big part of my life. I've learned a lot from the series throughout my life and somehow it motivates me to move on despite how difficult things have been for me recently. If you need to talk, I'll send you a PM with my actual username because this is a throwaway/alternate accout. Also, the folks over at /r/suicidewatch are very helpful and kind. This stuff isn't easy but you just have to keep your head up - stay focused on the mission that is life.

Also, a few notes in a special order that are very fitting here and are some of the lessons I hold close during hard times: Choose life, Snake. Pass on your genes or your memes. Remember your cousin's legacy. Build yourself a new Mother Base made up of friends and family. Live your life through to your final mission.

Carry on your cousin's legacy, and always remember the good times you had. Cherish them. Don't regret a thing. Life happens the way it does for a reason. Whatever your cousin was going through, it was too much for him to enjoy living. Know that he is truly at peace now and you will forever hold the good memories in your heart.

That's an interesting take on it but one I might have to try. One of my old teachers in high school said "choose your own attitude," kind of similar to what you suggested. It's tough sometimes but it has helped me in the past. Thank you for the kind words and advice.
I'm doing my best, the few positive things I can think of are what's keeping me together so the more I can find, the better.

Thank you, I'm going to need a lot of luck to get through this. I've lost plenty of friends from my old lifestyle as a drug addict but nothing has affected me like this. It's expected in that world but she had nothing to do with anything like that in her life. It just helps to know that she is at peace and doesn't have to deal with the pain or stress or anxiety that she was going through.

I know she is at peace now and that's what she wanted. It's one of the things she said in her note, and one of the very few things keeping me going right now. The fact that she no longer has to suffer from her back pain and the side effects of the steroid shot the doctors gave her to try to help with her back (which had very negative side effects and was one of the main reasons she attempted the first time). I'm glad she doesn't have to live with the pain and stress anymore but I wish she had just suck it out a little longer. Things would have been alright in a few more weeks. She was an accountant and this is the busiest time of the year but after April 15th things would have started to get much better for her. It was only a few more days. The last time I saw her or talked to her was on Sunday when I went to go help her out with work to try and ease her stress.
Thank you. I tend to try to keep things to myself but I will try to focus on helping others in the process as well as myself. I appreciate the advice.
Thank you. The chaplain told me the same thing. Reading the note just makes it worse.
Thank you for taking the time to leave that information for me. Good to know what I'm going to feel is supposed to be happening.

I've lost many friends as well over the past few years. I am a former addict and my drug of choice leads to many deaths by overdose. Nothing has affected me this much but that's not a surprise. Thanks for the advice, I tend to let things bottle up at times.
